evals.name: audit-form-with-planted-defects
evals.prompt: Here's the signup form for my landscaping business (signup.html). Can you check it over before I put it live? We're going to start texting people about seasonal offers.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the pre-ticked box, the required marketing consent, and the bundling of terms with marketing permission as blocking/serious. Gives replacement HTML. Flags that it is not legal advice without drowning the findings.

assertions.text: Flags the pre-ticked consent checkbox as a blocking defect
Flags that marketing consent is required to submit
Flags terms acceptance bundled with marketing consent
Provides literal replacement text or HTML, not just a description of the problem
States it is not legal advice
Names specific items for a lawyer rather than only a blanket disclaimer

evals.name: outbound-ai-calling-b2b-assumption
evals.prompt: We want our AI voice agent to call small businesses in our city from a list we bought, to pitch our service. It's all B2B so TCPA doesn't apply, right? Just need to know what to put on the website form.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the B2B misconception (no exemption for mobile numbers; small business owners answer on mobiles). Explains a bought list carries no consent. Covers artificial-voice call requirements. Recommends counsel before launch.

assertions.text: Corrects the claim that B2B is exempt from the TCPA
Explains that a purchased list carries no prior express written consent
States that an AI voice counts as an artificial voice
Covers the outbound call disclosure requirements (identity at the start, opt-out)
Recommends a lawyer before running the campaign

evals.name: draft-privacy-retention-and-sharing
evals.prompt: I run a small dental practice and we just started using an AI phone assistant that books appointments and records calls. I need a privacy policy section covering what we keep and who we share it with. We use Google Calendar, Mailchimp, and the AI vendor.
evals.expected_output: Produces a drafted section with a retention table using concrete periods and a vendor table including the AI vendor. Flags health data as a regulated category needing counsel (HIPAA). Notes call recording consent.

assertions.text: Produces drafted policy text, not just advice about what to include
States concrete retention periods rather than 'as long as necessary'
Lists the AI vendor as a recipient of personal data
Flags health data as a regulated category requiring specialist review
Addresses consent for call recording or transcription
